verses.restored: Samson went to Gaza and saw there a woman who was a sex worker, and he went in to her.

familiar.text: Then went Samson to Gaza, and saw there an harlot, and went in unto her.

modern.text: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן עַזָּ֑תָה וַיַּרְא שָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: It was said to Gazites, Samson has come here. They surrounded and lay in wait for him all night at gate of city. They kept silent all night, saying, Until light of morning—then we will kill him.

familiar.text: And it was told the Gazites, saying, Samson is come hither. And they compassed him in, and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and were quiet all the night, saying, In the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.

modern.text: When the Gazites heard that Samson was there, they surrounded that place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They were quiet throughout the night, saying, “Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.”

original.text: לַֽעַזָּתִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֗ר בָּ֤א שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ הֵ֔נָּה וַיָּסֹ֛בּוּ וַיֶּאֶרְבוּ ל֥וֹ כָל הַלַּ֖יְלָה בְּשַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיִּתְחָרְשׁ֤וּ כָל הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עַד א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר וַהֲרְגְנֻֽהוּ

verses.restored: Samson lay until half of night. He rose at half of night, grasped doors of gate of city and two doorposts, pulled them out with bar, set them upon his shoulders, and brought them up to top of hill that faces Hebron.

familiar.text: And Samson lay till midnight, and arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, and put them upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron.

modern.text: But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron. Samson and Delilah

verses.restored: After this, he loved a woman in wadi of Sorek, and her name was Delilah.

familiar.text: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

modern.text: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב אִשָּׁ֖ה בְּנַ֣חַל שֹׂרֵ֑ק וּשְׁמָ֖הּ דְּלִילָֽה

verses.restored: Lords of Philistines came up to her and said to her, Entice him and see by what his strength is great, and by what we can prevail over him, so we may bind him to afflict/humiliate him. We each will give you eleven hundred silver.

familiar.text: And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him: and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.

modern.text: The lords of the Philistines went to her and said, “Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him. Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver. ”

verses.restored: Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, please, by what your strength is great, and with what you may be bound to afflict you.

familiar.text: And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee.

modern.text: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הַגִּֽידָה נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֣ גָד֑וֹל וּבַמֶּ֥ה תֵאָסֵ֖ר לְעַנּוֹתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Samson said to her, If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I shall become weak and be like one human.

familiar.text: And Samson said unto her, If they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak, and be as another man.

modern.text: Samson told her, “If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִם יַאַסְרֻ֗נִי בְּשִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא חֹרָ֑בוּ וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם

verses.restored: Lords of Philistines brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

familiar.text: Then the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven green withs which had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

modern.text: So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him up with them.

original.text: וַיַּעֲלוּ לָ֞הּ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים שִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא חֹרָ֑בוּ וַתַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בָּהֶֽם

verses.restored: The ambush was sitting for her in inner room. She said to him, Philistines are upon you, Samson! He snapped bowstrings as thread of flax is snapped when it smells fire, and his strength was not known.

familiar.text: Now there were men lying in wait, abiding with her in the chamber. And she said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he brake the withs, as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire. So his strength was not known.

modern.text: While the men were hidden in her room, she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he snapped the bowstrings like a strand of yarn seared by a flame. So the source of his strength remained unknown.

modern.text: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.”

verses.restored: He said to her, If binding, they bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, I shall become weak and be like one human.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, If they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak, and be as another man.

modern.text: He replied, “If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.”

verses.restored: Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them. She said to him, Philistines are upon you, Samson! The ambush was sitting in inner room, and he snapped them from upon his arms like a thread.

familiar.text: Delilah therefore took new ropes, and bound him therewith, and said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And there were liers in wait abiding in the chamber. And he brake them from off his arms like a thread.

modern.text: So Delilah took new ropes, tied him up with them, and called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But while the men were hidden in her room, he snapped the ropes off his arms like they were threads.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח דְּלִילָה֩ עֲבֹתִ֨ים חֲדָשִׁ֜ים וַתַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בָהֶ֗ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֤ים עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וְהָאֹרֵ֖ב יֹשֵׁ֣ב בֶּחָ֑דֶר וַֽיְנַתְּקֵ֛ם מֵעַ֥ל זְרֹעֹתָ֖יו כַּחֽוּט

verses.restored: Delilah said to Samson, Until now you have mocked me and spoken lies to me. Tell me with what you may be bound. He said to her, If you weave seven locks of my head with web.

familiar.text: And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.

modern.text: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me all along! Tell me how you can be tied up.” He told her, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man. ”

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר דְּלִילָ֜ה אֶל שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן עַד הֵ֜נָּה הֵתַ֤לְתָּ בִּי֙ וַתְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַי֙ כְּזָבִ֔ים הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם תַּאַרְגִ֗י אֶת שֶׁ֛בַע מַחְלְפ֥וֹת רֹאשִׁ֖י עִם הַמַּסָּֽכֶת

verses.restored: She fastened with pin and said to him, Philistines are upon you, Samson! He awoke from his sleep and pulled away pin of loom and web.

familiar.text: And she fastened it with the pin, and said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awaked out of his sleep, and went away with the pin of the beam, and with the web.

modern.text: So while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the web. Then she tightened it with a pin and called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin with the loom and the web. Delilah Learns the Secret

original.text: וַתִּתְקַע֙ בַּיָּתֵ֔ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּיקַץ֙ מִשְּׁנָת֔וֹ וַיִּסַּ֛ע אֶת הַיְתַ֥ד הָאֶ֖רֶג וְאֶת הַמַּסָּֽכֶת

verses.restored: She said to him, How can you say, I love you, when your heart is not with me? These three times you have mocked me and have not told me by what your strength is great.

familiar.text: And she said unto him, How canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? thou hast mocked me these three times, and hast not told me wherein thy great strength lieth.

modern.text: “How can you say, ‘I love you,’” she asked, “when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me and failed to reveal to me the source of your great strength!”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֚יךְ תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ וְלִבְּךָ֖ אֵ֣ין אִתִּ֑י זֶ֣ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וְלֹא הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֥ גָדֽוֹל

verses.restored: When she pressed him with her words all days and urged him, his soul/life was shortened to death.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death;

modern.text: Finally, after she had pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death,

original.text: וַ֠יְהִי כִּֽי הֵצִ֨יקָה לּ֧וֹ בִדְבָרֶ֛יהָ כָּל הַיָּמִ֖ים וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נַפְשׁ֖וֹ לָמֽוּת

verses.restored: He told her all his heart and said to her, A razor has not gone up over my head, because a Nazirite of Divine I am from womb of my mother. If I am shaved, my strength will turn aside from me, and I shall become weak and be like every human.

familiar.text: That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.

modern.text: Samson told her all that was in his heart: “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.”

original.text: וַיַּגֶּד לָ֣הּ אֶת כָּל לִבּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מוֹרָה֙ לֹֽא עָלָ֣ה עַל רֹאשִׁ֔י כִּֽי נְזִ֧יר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲנִ֖י מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֑י אִם גֻּלַּ֨חְתִּי֙ וְסָ֣ר מִמֶּ֣נִּי כֹחִ֔י וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּכָל הָאָדָֽם

verses.restored: Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart. She sent and called lords of Philistines, saying, Come up this time, because he has told me all his heart. Lords of Philistines came up to her and brought silver in their hand.

familiar.text: And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, saying, Come up this once, for he hath shewed me all his heart. Then the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and brought money in their hand.

modern.text: When Delilah realized that he had revealed to her all that was in his heart, she sent this message to the lords of the Philistines: “Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.” Then the lords of the Philistines came to her, bringing the money in their hands.

verses.restored: She made him sleep upon her knees, called to a man, and he shaved seven locks of his head. She began to afflict/humiliate him, and his strength turned aside from upon him.

familiar.text: And she made him sleep upon her knees; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.

modern.text: And having lulled him to sleep on her lap, she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head. In this way she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.

verses.restored: She said, Philistines are upon you, Samson! He awoke from his sleep and said, I will go out as time after time and shake myself free. He did not know that YHWH had turned aside from upon him.

familiar.text: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was departed from him.

modern.text: Then she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” When Samson awoke from his sleep, he thought, “I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.

original.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּקַ֣ץ מִשְּׁנָת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵצֵ֞א כְּפַ֤עַם בְּפַ֨עַם֙ וְאִנָּעֵ֔ר וְהוּא֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza, bound him with double bronze fetters, and he was grinding in house of prisoners.

modern.text: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison.

translation_notes: The Gaza sex worker is not named or blamed. The verse reports Samson's visit without making her a symbol of sexual corruption, and it gives no permission to stigmatize sex workers.
Samson's removal of the Gaza gate is a feat of humiliation against a city and a display of power, not a model for trespass, property destruction, or invulnerability.

Delilah is named and is approached by Philistine rulers with a large payment. The text does not state her ethnicity, motives beyond the arrangement, or whether additional pressure was applied; avoid both misogynistic demonization and unsupported exoneration.

Delilah explicitly asks how Samson can be bound 'to afflict/humiliate' him. Samson remains through repeated binding attempts and lies repeatedly. The relationship is unsafe, manipulative, and coercive; neither danger nor abuse should be romanticized as passion.
Verses 13-14 are textually difficult and appear compressed in the Masoretic Text; Greek witnesses preserve additional weaving details. Later audit should compare witnesses.

'His soul was shortened to death' describes extreme emotional exhaustion under relentless pressure. It must not be used to excuse coercion, blame victims for disclosure, or normalize wearing down a partner's boundaries.

Samson's hair is the embodied sign of Nazirite consecration, not a magic object independent of covenant identity. The narrative says YHWH had turned aside, not that disability or shaved appearance makes a person spiritually empty.
The gouging of Samson's eyes is torture and deliberate disability-making. Acquired blindness is not shame, punishment inherent in disability, moral contamination, or loss of personhood.
Grinding in prison is forced labor. The later public performance is captivity abuse and disability humiliation, not harmless entertainment.
The boy holding Samson's hand functions as a guide. Receiving guidance or access support is not infantilization or evidence that a blind person lacks agency.

The temple contains rulers and a large mixed crowd of men and women, including people on the roof. The collapse is mass killing with likely noncombatants present; it cannot be reduced to a clean strike against military leaders.
Samson's prayer is explicitly revenge for his eyes. Divine response in a tragic narrative does not turn vengeance or mass death into a universal command.
'Let my life die with Philistines' is a self-involving act of mass killing. It must never be preached as noble suicide, holy martyrdom, proof of faith, or permission to die while harming others.
Samson's family retrieves and buries him, restoring kinship and burial dignity after public degradation. Burial does not erase the devastation of his final act.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not eroticize coercion, blame all women through Delilah, shame sex workers, equate blindness with spiritual failure, mock disability, or romanticize captivity. Do not glamorize revenge, mass killing, self-destruction, martyrdom, or suicide through Samson's death. This ending is tragedy: a tortured captive kills himself and a crowded building of people. It is not a template for personal, political, or religious action.
